address-interchange.quote: For chunk values $H,D$,

address-interchange.name: chunk digits
address-interchange.meaning: The number of radix-q digits in each chunk.
address-interchange.quote: Let each chunk have $e=m^k$ digits ($k$ recursion levels).

address-interchange.name: level count
address-interchange.meaning: The number of recursion levels, with e=m^k.
address-interchange.quote: Let each chunk have $e=m^k$ digits ($k$ recursion levels).

address-interchange.name: field digits
address-interchange.meaning: The number of digits in each of the m fields of a chunk.
address-interchange.quote: Cut it into $m$ fields of $b=e/m$ digits

address-interchange.name: vertex matrix
address-interchange.meaning: The rational m by m matrix assigned to a terminal or gate.
address-interchange.quote: each terminal and gate carries a rational $m\times m$ matrix $M$

address-interchange.name: edge index
address-interchange.meaning: Index of an edge of the network.
address-interchange.quote: and edge $i$ carries $A_i=M_{\mathrm{head}(i)}-M_{\mathrm{tail}(i)}$

address-interchange.name: edge matrix
address-interchange.meaning: The difference of the matrices at the head and tail of edge i.
address-interchange.quote: and edge $i$ carries $A_i=M_{\mathrm{head}(i)}-M_{\mathrm{tail}(i)}$

address-interchange.name: identity matrix
address-interchange.meaning: The m by m identity matrix.
address-interchange.quote: $M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}=I_m$ (the identity)

address-interchange.name: wire index
address-interchange.meaning: The index of a wire of the network, 1 to W.
address-interchange.quote: The shear contract: input wire $w$ ends at output role $\rho(w)$

address-interchange.name: shear permutation
address-interchange.meaning: The array permutation moving the entry at address (H,D) to (H+MD,D).
address-interchange.quote: Let $\Phi_M$ move the entry at address $(H,D)$ to $(H+MD,D)$.

address-interchange.name: other matrix
address-interchange.meaning: Another rational m by m matrix.
address-interchange.quote: For another matrix $M'$,

address-interchange.name: stream row
address-interchange.meaning: The row number within a role stream.
address-interchange.quote: row $Wx+w-1$ goes to stream $w$ as row $x$

address-interchange.name: input array
address-interchange.meaning: The physical input array on wire w.
address-interchange.quote: Read wire $w$'s input $f_w$ as the logical array

address-interchange.name: output array
address-interchange.meaning: The physical output array at role rho(w).
address-interchange.quote: the output is $f'_{\rho(w)}=\Phi_{M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}}\Phi_{-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}}f_w=\Phi_{I_m}f_w$

address-interchange.name: level
address-interchange.meaning: Index of a level of the unrolled recurrence.
address-interchange.quote: Unrolled over levels $j$,

address-interchange.name: normalized cost
address-interchange.meaning: The time per unit volume of the interchange at width m^k.
address-interchange.quote: The time per unit volume $F_k$ at width $m^k$ obeys

address-interchange.name: level count
address-interchange.meaning: The least integer with m^{k'} at least e.
address-interchange.quote: put $k'=\lceil\log_m e\rceil$

address-interchange.name: top digits
address-interchange.meaning: The number of top digits of each chunk interchanged first.
address-interchange.quote: and $\nu=\lceil k'\log W/(2\log q)\rceil$

address-interchange.name: high part of h
address-interchange.meaning: The top nu digits of the first chunk.
address-interchange.quote: Split each chunk into top $\nu$ digits and rest, $h^+,h^-$ and $d^+,d^-$.

address-interchange.name: rest of h
address-interchange.meaning: The remaining digits of the first chunk.
address-interchange.quote: Split each chunk into top $\nu$ digits and rest, $h^+,h^-$ and $d^+,d^-$.

address-interchange.name: high part of d
address-interchange.meaning: The top nu digits of the second chunk.
address-interchange.quote: Split each chunk into top $\nu$ digits and rest, $h^+,h^-$ and $d^+,d^-$.

address-interchange.name: rest of d
address-interchange.meaning: The remaining digits of the second chunk.
address-interchange.quote: Split each chunk into top $\nu$ digits and rest, $h^+,h^-$ and $d^+,d^-$.

address-interchange.name: row range
address-interchange.meaning: The range of the row field formed by the two high parts.
address-interchange.quote: Now $d^+,h^+$ form a row field of range $\Lambda=q^{2\nu}\ge W^{k'}$ before both remaining chunks.

address-interchange.name: padded row range
address-interchange.meaning: The row count after padding with zero rows.
address-interchange.quote: Pad with zero rows to $\Lambda'=W^{k'}\lceil \Lambda/W^{k'}\rceil<2\Lambda$ rows

address-interchange.name: piece count
address-interchange.meaning: The number of pieces of width m^j, the j-th base-m digit of e minus nu.
address-interchange.quote: Write $e-\nu=\sum_{j=0}^{k'}a_jm^j$, $0\le a_j<m$.

array-frames.name: scalar ring
array-frames.meaning: The ring of scalars carried by the wires.
array-frames.quote: Let $R$ be the ring of scalars carried by the wires, and let $\Omega$ be a finite set of addresses indexing every array.

array-frames.name: address set
array-frames.meaning: A finite set of addresses indexing every array.
array-frames.quote: Let $R$ be the ring of scalars carried by the wires, and let $\Omega$ be a finite set of addresses indexing every array.

array-frames.name: frame
array-frames.meaning: The invertible R-linear operator on R^Omega assigned to a source, gate or sink v.
array-frames.quote: At each source, gate and sink $v$, assign an invertible $R$-linear operator $D_v$ on $R^\Omega$, called its frame.

array-frames.name: gate input count
array-frames.meaning: The number of input arrays of a gate.
array-frames.quote: At a gate $G$ with $t$ input arrays, every incoming array has the common frame $D_v$, and a gate output combines the logical inputs $\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_t$ with coefficients $c_j\in R$.

butterfly.name: transform length
butterfly.meaning: The number of positions in the sequence being transformed, a power of two.
butterfly.quote: Here $t$ is the transform length, a power of two.

butterfly.name: input value
butterfly.meaning: The input value at position k of the sequence being transformed.
butterfly.quote: Let $z_k$, for positions $0\le k<t$, be the input values, and let $\omega_t=e^{2\pi i/t}$.

butterfly.name: output index
butterfly.meaning: The index of an output of the transform.
butterfly.quote: The transform is $(F_tz)_m=\frac1t\sum_j z_j\omega_t^{-jm}$, where $m$ is the output index.

butterfly.name: lowest bit
butterfly.meaning: The lowest bit of the output index m.
butterfly.quote: Write $m=2h+b$, where $b\in\{0,1\}$ is the lowest bit of $m$ and $h$ is the remaining index.

butterfly.name: remaining index
butterfly.meaning: The output index m with its lowest bit removed.
butterfly.quote: Write $m=2h+b$, where $b\in\{0,1\}$ is the lowest bit of $m$ and $h$ is the remaining index.

chirp.name: output index
chirp.meaning: The index tuple (j_1,...,j_d) of an entry of the data and of the output position.
chirp.quote: Index the data by $\boldsymbol j=(j_1,\dots,j_d)$, where $d$ is the number of axes.

chirp.name: source length
chirp.meaning: An integer coprime to t_i attached to axis i, the multiplier of the frequency read.
chirp.quote: On axis $i$, $t_i$ is the even number of entries along that axis and $s_i$ is an integer coprime to $t_i$.

chirp.name: frequency
chirp.meaning: The frequency tuple (f_1,...,f_d) labelling an output entry of the transform.
chirp.quote: The transform is $(F_{\boldsymbol t}u)_{\boldsymbol f}=\frac1T\sum_{\boldsymbol k}u_{\boldsymbol k}\exp(-2\pi i\sum_i k_if_i/t_i)$, where $\boldsymbol f=(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ is the frequency labelling an output entry.

chirp.name: target permutation
chirp.meaning: The permutation of the output so that position j holds the entry of frequency (-s_i j_i)_i.
chirp.quote: The target permutation $Q$ reorders the output so that position $\boldsymbol j$ holds the entry of frequency $(-s_ij_i)_i$.

chirp.name: chirp
chirp.meaning: The array of phases a_j = exp(-pi i sum s_i j_i^2/t_i), quadratic in the index.
chirp.quote: Define the chirp $a_{\boldsymbol j}=\exp\left(-\pi i\sum_{i=1}^d s_ij_i^2/t_i\right)$, a phase quadratic in the index, and let $\overline a$ be its complex conjugate.

conjecture.name: bit length
conjecture.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two integers being multiplied.
conjecture.quote: The Schönhage–Strassen optimality conjecture is the claim that $n\log n$ is the best possible order of growth for the time to multiply two integers, where $n$ is the number of bits in each; it is the statement that the main result of this wiki disproves.

conjecture.name: machine constant
conjecture.meaning: A positive constant, depending on the machine, in the lower bound c n log n.
conjecture.quote: This is a lower-bound statement, not a claim about one algorithm: for every multiplication machine there are a constant $c>0$ and a threshold such that the machine needs at least $c\,n\log n$ steps whenever $n$ exceeds the threshold.

conjecture.name: power saving
conjecture.meaning: A fixed positive constant by which the exponent of the logarithm is lowered.
conjecture.quote: Its running time is $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$, where $\kappa>0$ is a fixed constant, the amount by which the exponent of the logarithm is lowered.

contraction-maps.name: linear map
contraction-maps.meaning: A linear map whose norm bound is being defined.
contraction-maps.quote: A linear map $L$ is a *contraction* if $\|Lu\|\le\|u\|$ for every $u$.

contraction-maps.name: bilinear map
contraction-maps.meaning: A map linear in each of its two operands.
contraction-maps.quote: A map $\mathcal M(f,g)$ that is linear in each operand $f$ and $g$ separately is a *bilinear contraction* if $\|\mathcal M(f,g)\|\le\|f\|\,\|g\|$.

contraction-maps.name: first operand
contraction-maps.meaning: The first operand of the bilinear map.
contraction-maps.quote: A map $\mathcal M(f,g)$ that is linear in each operand $f$ and $g$ separately is a *bilinear contraction* if $\|\mathcal M(f,g)\|\le\|f\|\,\|g\|$.

contraction-maps.name: second operand
contraction-maps.meaning: The second operand of the bilinear map.
contraction-maps.quote: A map $\mathcal M(f,g)$ that is linear in each operand $f$ and $g$ separately is a *bilinear contraction* if $\|\mathcal M(f,g)\|\le\|f\|\,\|g\|$.

contraction-maps.name: computed input
contraction-maps.meaning: A computed approximation replacing the exact input u.
contraction-maps.quote: Suppose a computed input $u'$ replaces the exact input $u$.

contraction-maps.name: perturbed first operand
contraction-maps.meaning: A perturbed replacement for the operand f.
contraction-maps.quote: For a bilinear contraction, replace operands $f,g$ by $f',g'$.

contraction-maps.name: perturbed second operand
contraction-maps.meaning: A perturbed replacement for the operand g.
contraction-maps.quote: For a bilinear contraction, replace operands $f,g$ by $f',g'$.

contraction-maps.name: normalized transform
contraction-maps.meaning: The normalized discrete Fourier transform on sequences of q entries.
contraction-maps.quote: where $F_q$ is the transform on sequences of $q$ entries.

controlled-shifts.name: prime
controlled-shifts.meaning: The prime base of the digits of a field.
controlled-shifts.quote: Fix a prime $q$ (on this page $q$ is a prime, not a sequence length), and let $b\ge1$ be the number of base-$q$ digits of a field.

controlled-shifts.name: digits per field
controlled-shifts.meaning: The number of base-q digits of a field.
controlled-shifts.quote: Fix a prime $q$ (on this page $q$ is a prime, not a sequence length), and let $b\ge1$ be the number of base-$q$ digits of a field.

controlled-shifts.name: field values
controlled-shifts.meaning: The number of values a field can take, q^b.
controlled-shifts.quote: Put $Q=q^b$, the number of values a field can take, and let $V$ be the array volume, the number of stored data bits.

controlled-shifts.name: target value
controlled-shifts.meaning: The value of the target field, in [Q].
controlled-shifts.quote: The target field has value $y\in[Q]=\{0,\dots,Q-1\}$ and follows a fixed number of control fields.

controlled-shifts.name: offset
controlled-shifts.meaning: The offset added to the target, prepared from the control values.
controlled-shifts.quote: where $a\in[Q]$ is the offset, prepared from the control values.

controlled-shifts.name: suffix bits
controlled-shifts.meaning: The number of bits following the target field.
controlled-shifts.quote: If $B$ bits follow the target, the target and its suffix form $Q$ consecutive blocks of $B$ bits.

controlled-shifts.name: multiplier
controlled-shifts.meaning: A fixed positive integer prime to q by which the target is multiplied.
controlled-shifts.quote: Let $c$ be a fixed positive integer prime to $q$.

controlled-shifts.name: piece index
controlled-shifts.meaning: The index of the increasing piece of y -> cy mod Q containing y.
controlled-shifts.quote: The map $y\mapsto cy \pmod Q$ consists of $c$ increasing pieces, indexed by $j=\lfloor cy/Q\rfloor$.

controlled-shifts.name: output coordinate
controlled-shifts.meaning: The output coordinate of the target after scaling, running from 0 to Q-1.
controlled-shifts.quote: Split the blocks into $c$ streams by $j$, then produce output coordinates $y'=0,\dots,Q-1$ in order, taking each block from the stream $j$ with $y'+jQ\equiv 0\pmod c$, where $y=(y'+jQ)/c$.

controlled-shifts.name: denominator
controlled-shifts.meaning: The positive integer denominator, prime to q, of a rational unit.
controlled-shifts.quote: A rational unit is a signed ratio $c/c'$ of positive integers $c,c'$ both prime to $q$.

controlled-shifts.name: array volume
controlled-shifts.meaning: The number of stored data bits in the array.
controlled-shifts.quote: Put $Q=q^b$, the number of values a field can take, and let $V$ be the array volume, the number of stored data bits.

convolution.name: sequence length
convolution.meaning: The number of entries in each sequence being convolved.
convolution.quote: For two sequences $f,g$ indexed by $\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z$, where $q$ is the number of entries in each sequence, the cyclic convolution is

convolution.name: axis count
convolution.meaning: One more than the number of cyclic axes of an array.
convolution.quote: The algorithm uses arrays with $d-1$ cyclic axes, where $d$ is one more than the number of cyclic axes and $t_i$ is the length of cyclic axis $i$.

convolution.name: axis length
convolution.meaning: The length of cyclic axis i.
convolution.quote: The algorithm uses arrays with $d-1$ cyclic axes, where $d$ is one more than the number of cyclic axes and $t_i$ is the length of cyclic axis $i$.

convolution.name: cyclic address count
convolution.meaning: The number of addresses on the cyclic axes of an array.
convolution.quote: Let $M=\prod_{i<d}t_i$ be the number of cyclic addresses, and $T=rM$ the total number of complex coefficients in an array.

convolution.name: total coefficient count
convolution.meaning: The total number of complex coefficients in an array.
convolution.quote: Let $M=\prod_{i<d}t_i$ be the number of cyclic addresses, and $T=rM$ the total number of complex coefficients in an array.

cost-accounting.name: volume
cost-accounting.meaning: The volume, the total number of bits of the T coefficients of p bits each, Tp = Theta(n).
cost-accounting.quote: Let $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$ be the volume of $T$ coefficients of $p$ bits.

cost-accounting.name: margin
cost-accounting.meaning: The margin below one of the i-th dominant normalized cost, a positive number with that cost equal to p^{1-g_i}.
cost-accounting.quote: Each is a power $p^{1-g_i}$, where $g_i>0$ is its margin below one.

cost-accounting.name: visit exponent
cost-accounting.meaning: A fixed exponent such that there are at most p^A setup visits in the recursions.
cost-accounting.quote: The recursions have constant branching and depth $O(\log p)$, so fix exponents $A$ and $C$ with at most $p^A$ visits, each with setup of at most $p^C$ steps.

cost-accounting.name: setup exponent
cost-accounting.meaning: A fixed exponent such that the setup of one visit takes at most p^C steps.
cost-accounting.quote: The recursions have constant branching and depth $O(\log p)$, so fix exponents $A$ and $C$ with at most $p^A$ visits, each with setup of at most $p^C$ steps.

crt-map.name: convolution length
crt-map.meaning: The length of the cyclic convolution, the product of the s_i.
crt-map.quote: The Chinese-remainder address map rewrites a cyclic convolution of length $S=s_1\cdots s_d$ as a multidimensional one, moving the data on tape by controlled shifts only.

crt-map.name: number of axes
crt-map.meaning: The number of axes of the target ring.
crt-map.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes, $i$ index them, and the lengths $s_i$ be pairwise coprime (unrelated to $s_i$ on the chirp page).

crt-map.name: axis index
crt-map.meaning: The index of an axis, from 1 to d.
crt-map.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes, $i$ index them, and the lengths $s_i$ be pairwise coprime (unrelated to $s_i$ on the chirp page).

crt-map.name: axis source length
crt-map.meaning: The length of axis i, pairwise coprime with the others; unrelated to the s_i of the chirp page.
crt-map.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes, $i$ index them, and the lengths $s_i$ be pairwise coprime (unrelated to $s_i$ on the chirp page).

crt-map.name: prefix product
crt-map.meaning: The product of the lengths s_j of the axes before axis i.
crt-map.quote: Let $P_i=\prod_{j<i}s_j$ be the product of the lengths before axis $i$, and $\mu_i=P_i^{-1}\pmod{s_i}$.

crt-map.name: coordinate exponent
crt-map.meaning: The inverse of P_i modulo s_i.
crt-map.quote: Let $P_i=\prod_{j<i}s_j$ be the product of the lengths before axis $i$, and $\mu_i=P_i^{-1}\pmod{s_i}$.

crt-map.name: axis variable
crt-map.meaning: The polynomial variable of axis i, with x_i^{s_i}=1.
crt-map.quote: Define $\Phi:\mathbb C[x]/(x^S-1)\to\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_i^{s_i}-1)$ by $x\mapsto\prod_i x_i^{\mu_i}$, with one variable $x_i$ per axis. Since $s_i\mid S$, each $x_i^{\mu_iS}=1$, so $\Phi$ respects $x^S=1$ and defines an algebra map.

crt-map.name: Chinese-remainder map
crt-map.meaning: The ring isomorphism sending x to the product of x_i^{mu_i}.
crt-map.quote: Define $\Phi:\mathbb C[x]/(x^S-1)\to\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_i^{s_i}-1)$ by $x\mapsto\prod_i x_i^{\mu_i}$, with one variable $x_i$ per axis. Since $s_i\mid S$, each $x_i^{\mu_iS}=1$, so $\Phi$ respects $x^S=1$ and defines an algebra map.

crt-map.name: coefficient index
crt-map.meaning: The index of a coefficient of the length-S sequence.
crt-map.quote: For an exponent $k$, the index of a coefficient, $\Phi(x^k)=1$ exactly when $s_i\mid\mu_ik$ for every $i$; as $\mu_i$ is a unit modulo $s_i$ this means $s_i\mid k$ for every $i$, and as the $s_i$ are pairwise coprime, $S\mid k$.

crt-map.name: mixed-radix digit
crt-map.meaning: The j-th digit of k in mixed radix, 0 <= a_j < s_j.
crt-map.quote: Write $k=\sum_ja_jP_j$ in mixed radix with digits $0\le a_j<s_j$.

crt-map.name: axis coordinate
crt-map.quote: The axis-$i$ coordinate $b_i$ of $\Phi(x^k)$ is $\mu_ik\bmod s_i$.

crt-map.name: padded axis length
crt-map.meaning: The padded length of axis i, either r/2 or r.
crt-map.quote: Pad axis $i$ with zero records to a length $t_i\in\{r/2,r\}$, where $r=2^\ell$ is the record length.

crt-map.name: address bits
crt-map.meaning: The base-2 logarithm of the record length r, the number of address bits of a full-width axis.
crt-map.quote: Pad axis $i$ with zero records to a length $t_i\in\{r/2,r\}$, where $r=2^\ell$ is the record length.

crt-map.name: padded record count
crt-map.meaning: The number of padded records, the product of the t_i.
crt-map.quote: Let $T=\prod_it_i$ be the number of padded records, each of $O(p)$ bits (with $p$ as on the fixed-point page).

crt-map.name: stream volume
crt-map.meaning: The volume of the stream being moved, Tp bits.
crt-map.quote: Let $V=Tp$ be the stream volume and $\tau<1$ a fixed exponent.

crt-map.name: chunk-swap exponent
crt-map.meaning: A fixed exponent below 1 in the cost of a chunk interchange.
crt-map.quote: Let $V=Tp$ be the stream volume and $\tau<1$ a fixed exponent.

dft.name: sequence length
dft.meaning: The number of entries of a sequence.
dft.quote: Let $q\ge 1$ be the number of entries of a sequence, and let $u=(u_0,\dots,u_{q-1})$ be a sequence of $q$ complex numbers, with subscripts taken modulo $q$.

dft.name: input sequence
dft.meaning: A sequence of q complex numbers to be transformed.
dft.quote: Let $q\ge 1$ be the number of entries of a sequence, and let $u=(u_0,\dots,u_{q-1})$ be a sequence of $q$ complex numbers, with subscripts taken modulo $q$.

dft.name: primitive root
dft.meaning: The primitive q-th root of unity e^{2\pi i/q}.
dft.quote: Writing $\omega = e^{2\pi i/q}$ for the primitive $q$-th root of unity, the weights are the powers $\omega^{-jk}$.

exchange-network.name: ground-set size
exchange-network.meaning: The size of the ground set [h] whose three-element subsets index the values.
exchange-network.quote: Fix the ground-set size $h=100$ and let $v=\binom h3=161700$ be the number of three-element subsets of $[h]$

exchange-network.name: triple count
exchange-network.meaning: The number of three-element subsets of [h].
exchange-network.quote: Fix the ground-set size $h=100$ and let $v=\binom h3=161700$ be the number of three-element subsets of $[h]$

exchange-network.name: triple set
exchange-network.meaning: The set of three-element subsets of [h].
exchange-network.quote: and let $\mathcal T$ be the set of these subsets

exchange-network.name: bank size
exchange-network.meaning: The size of each data bank.
exchange-network.quote: Set $N=v^3=4227952113000000$ for the size of each data bank, and $m=h^3=1000000$ for the label-space dimension used later.

exchange-network.name: label dimension
exchange-network.meaning: The dimension of the label space used later.
exchange-network.quote: Set $N=v^3=4227952113000000$ for the size of each data bank, and $m=h^3=1000000$ for the label-space dimension used later.

exchange-network.name: triple
exchange-network.meaning: A three-element subset of [h], indexing a value in a bank.
exchange-network.quote: Fixing two coordinates of $a$ leaves values $x_S,y_S$ indexed by triples $S\in\mathcal T$; $x$ and $y$ denote the vectors of all $x_S$ and all $y_S$.

exchange-network.name: source vector
exchange-network.meaning: The vector of all values x_S.
exchange-network.quote: Fixing two coordinates of $a$ leaves values $x_S,y_S$ indexed by triples $S\in\mathcal T$; $x$ and $y$ denote the vectors of all $x_S$ and all $y_S$.

exchange-network.name: target vector
exchange-network.meaning: The vector of all values y_S.
exchange-network.quote: Fixing two coordinates of $a$ leaves values $x_S,y_S$ indexed by triples $S\in\mathcal T$; $x$ and $y$ denote the vectors of all $x_S$ and all $y_S$.

exchange-network.name: other triple
exchange-network.meaning: A second triple, the index of a source value x_{S'}.
exchange-network.quote: Through central wires $C_i$, $i\in[h]$, gather adds $\sum_{S'\ni i}x_{S'}$ to $C_i$, with $S'$ another triple, and scatter adds $\sum_{i\in S}C_i$ to $y_S$.

exchange-network.name: bank index
exchange-network.meaning: The index of a value in a data bank, a triple of triples.
exchange-network.quote: Banks $X_a,Y_a$ are indexed by $a\in\mathcal T^3$, a triple of triples.

exchange-network.name: side scratch vector
exchange-network.meaning: The initial values of the side scratch wires.
exchange-network.quote: Let $\sigma,\gamma$ be the initial side and central scratch vectors; $\mathcal V,\mathcal G,\mathcal J,\mathcal R$ are the copy, gather, injection and scatter maps.

exchange-network.name: central scratch vector
exchange-network.meaning: The initial values of the central scratch wires.
exchange-network.quote: Let $\sigma,\gamma$ be the initial side and central scratch vectors; $\mathcal V,\mathcal G,\mathcal J,\mathcal R$ are the copy, gather, injection and scatter maps.

exchange-network.name: invocation count
exchange-network.quote: Three stages run $v^2$ invocations with own scratch wires, so there are $I=3v^2=78440670000$ invocations.

exchange-network.name: bit neighbours
exchange-network.meaning: The number of neighbours of a fixed triple in the bit construction.
exchange-network.quote: A fixed triple has $z_{\rm b}=3\binom{97}{2}=13968$ neighbours in the bit construction

exchange-network.name: complex neighbours
exchange-network.meaning: The number of neighbours of a fixed triple in the complex construction.
exchange-network.quote: It has $z_{\rm c}=\binom{97}{3}+3\cdot97=147731$ neighbours in the complex construction (intersection zero plus intersection two).

exchange-network.name: bit central wires
exchange-network.meaning: The number of central wires per invocation in the bit network.
exchange-network.quote: There are $c_{\rm b}=100$ central wires per invocation in the bit network and $c_{\rm c}=101$ in the complex one.

exchange-network.name: complex central wires
exchange-network.meaning: The number of central wires per invocation in the complex network.
exchange-network.quote: There are $c_{\rm b}=100$ central wires per invocation in the bit network and $c_{\rm c}=101$ in the complex one.

exchange-network.name: bit wire count
exchange-network.meaning: The number of wires of the bit network.

exchange-network.name: complex wire count

fixed-point.name: fractional bits

fixed-point.quote: Let $p$ be the number of fractional bits, so stored values lie on the grid $2^{-p}\mathbb Z[i]$.

fixed-point.name: depth
fixed-point.meaning: The number of operations in sequence since the layer began that produced a value.
fixed-point.quote: Let a value computed with $k$ operations in sequence since the layer began be said to have depth $k$.

fixed-point.name: reserved extra bits
fixed-point.meaning: The number of extra bits reserved, at least the maximal depth reached in the layer.
fixed-point.quote: Let $\Delta$ be the number of extra bits reserved, at least the maximal depth reached in the layer.

fixed-point.name: truncation
fixed-point.meaning: The truncation that drops the bits below 2^{-p} in each real and imaginary part, returning a record to the p-bit grid.

frequency-order.name: negacyclic ring
frequency-order.meaning: The ring of polynomials in y with r complex coefficients, modulo y^r+1.

frequency-order.name: bit reversal

main-result.name: input length
main-result.meaning: The number of bits in each input integer.
main-result.quote: Power-saving integer multiplication is the main result: for $n$, the number of bits in each input, and $\kappa=2^{-182}$, the exponent saved from the power of $\lg n$, a fixed Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$, which is $o(n\log n)$, so it refutes the [Schönhage–Strassen optimality conjecture](conjecture.md) in this model.

multiplication-algorithm.name: padded axis length

multiplication-algorithm.name: padded-axis transform

multiplication-algorithm.name: computed chirp transform

multiplication-algorithm.quote: The computed source transform $\widetilde{\mathscr F}$ applies the [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md) map $\mathcal A$, then $\widetilde{\mathscr C}$, then the map $\mathcal B_0$, then multiplies exactly by $2^\gamma$, where $\gamma$ is the resampling scale exponent; its exact counterpart $\mathscr F$ replaces each numerical routine by the exact map it approximates, giving $\mathscr F=2^\gamma\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A=RF_{\boldsymbol s}$, where $R$ is a retained permutation.

phase-twist.name: second array
phase-twist.meaning: The second complex array being convolved with f.
phase-twist.quote: Let $f$ and $g$ be two complex arrays with $d$ axes, the last of length $r$, and $T$ entries in all.

phase-twist.name: axis count
phase-twist.meaning: The number of axes of the arrays.
phase-twist.quote: Let $f$ and $g$ be two complex arrays with $d$ axes, the last of length $r$, and $T$ entries in all.

phase-twist.name: last-axis variable
phase-twist.meaning: The variable of the last cyclic axis.
phase-twist.quote: Convolution along the last axis is multiplication in $\mathbb C[x_d]/(x_d^r-1)$, where $x_d$ is the variable of that axis.

phase-twist.name: negacyclic ring
phase-twist.meaning: The ring of polynomials modulo y^r+1.
phase-twist.quote: The twist converts the last cyclic axis into the coordinate of the [Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1](ring-y.md), written $\mathcal R_r$, where $y^r=-1$ instead.

phase-twist.name: twist root
phase-twist.meaning: The primitive 2r-th root of unity e^{\pi i/r}, with zeta^r=-1.

phase-twist.name: twist map
phase-twist.meaning: The ring isomorphism from the cyclic ring to the negacyclic ring sending x_d to zeta y.
phase-twist.quote: Define the ring map $\Theta$ from $\mathbb C[x_d]/(x_d^r-1)$ to $\mathcal R_r$ by $x_d\mapsto\zeta y$.

phase-twist.name: coefficient index
phase-twist.meaning: An index of a coefficient (not an operation count).
phase-twist.quote: Here $k$ and $l$ index coefficients, not operations.

phase-twist.name: second coefficient index
phase-twist.meaning: An index of a coefficient of the second factor.
phase-twist.quote: Here $k$ and $l$ index coefficients, not operations.

phase-twist.name: wrapped position
phase-twist.meaning: The position k+l reduced modulo r.
phase-twist.quote: Take $k,l<r$ and write $k+l=j+hr$, with $j<r$ the resulting position and $h\in\{0,1\}$ the wrap indicator.

phase-twist.name: wrap indicator
phase-twist.meaning: Zero or one according to whether k+l wrapped past r.
phase-twist.quote: Take $k,l<r$ and write $k+l=j+hr$, with $j<r$ the resulting position and $h\in\{0,1\}$ the wrap indicator.

phase-twist.name: record reading
phase-twist.meaning: The map reading each line along the last axis as a polynomial in R_r.
phase-twist.quote: $\iota$ reads each line $(f_{\boldsymbol j,k})_k$ as the polynomial $\sum_k f_{\boldsymbol j,k}y^k$, giving an array of $M$ records in $\mathcal R_r$.

phase-twist.name: diagonal twist
phase-twist.meaning: The maps multiplying entry k of each line by zeta^{+-k}.
phase-twist.quote: Let $(D_\pm f)_{\boldsymbol j,k}=\zeta^{\pm k}f_{\boldsymbol j,k}$ multiply entry $k$ of each line by $\zeta^{\pm k}$.

phase-twist.name: ring convolution
phase-twist.meaning: Normalized convolution of the first d-1 axes over R_r, including division by T.
phase-twist.quote: Let $\mathcal M_r$ be the ring convolution of [Convolution from the retained transform layout](ring-convolution.md): it convolves the first $d-1$ axes over $\mathcal R_r$, dividing by $T$.

phase-twist.name: complex convolution
phase-twist.meaning: The normalized complex cyclic convolution of two arrays.
phase-twist.quote: The composite $\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}$, the normalized complex cyclic convolution, is

phase-twist.name: sup norm
phase-twist.meaning: The largest modulus of a scalar coefficient of f.
phase-twist.quote: Write $\|f\|$ for the sup norm of an array $f$: the largest modulus of a scalar coefficient.

precision-recovery.name: grid step
precision-recovery.quote: Let $h_p=2^{-p}$, $L=\log_2T$, $S\le T$; for large $n$, $T<8n/b$ gives $T<2^b$ and $L<b$.

precision-recovery.name: log of padded size
precision-recovery.quote: Let $h_p=2^{-p}$, $L=\log_2T$, $S\le T$; for large $n$, $T<8n/b$ gives $T<2^b$ and $L<b$.

precision-recovery.name: ring convolution error
precision-recovery.meaning: The error bound of the ring convolution, M(3L+2).
precision-recovery.quote: Its transforms and truncation err by under $3L+2$ before a final exact multiplication by $M=T/r$, giving $E_{\rm ring}:=M(3L+2)<5TL$.

precision-recovery.name: axis lengths
precision-recovery.quote: The chirp transform $\widetilde{\mathscr C}$ evaluates the [Bluestein chirp identity](chirp.md), with $\boldsymbol t$ the axis lengths, $F_{\boldsymbol t}$ the exact Fourier transform and $Q$ the target permutation:

precision-recovery.name: exact Fourier transform
precision-recovery.meaning: The exact Fourier transform with axis lengths t.
precision-recovery.quote: The chirp transform $\widetilde{\mathscr C}$ evaluates the [Bluestein chirp identity](chirp.md), with $\boldsymbol t$ the axis lengths, $F_{\boldsymbol t}$ the exact Fourier transform and $Q$ the target permutation:

precision-recovery.name: source scale exponent
precision-recovery.meaning: The exponent of the source scale 2^gamma.
precision-recovery.quote: A source transform applies [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md) maps and a chirp transform (error under $2dp^2+8TL$), then scales exactly by the source scale $2^\gamma$ ($b\ge2^{24}$ gives $\gamma\le b/4$).

precision-recovery.name: source transform error
precision-recovery.meaning: The error bound, in units of h_p, of a source transform.
precision-recovery.quote: As $2dp^2<TL$ eventually, error is under $E_sh_p$, $E_s=9\cdot2^\gamma TL$.

precision-recovery.name: scaled digit array
precision-recovery.meaning: The array of scaled digits of the first input.
precision-recovery.quote: Here $u,v$ denote the scaled digit arrays (letters redefined): a digit $a$ is stored as $a2^{-b-2}$, norm under $1/4$.

precision-recovery.name: scaled digit array
precision-recovery.meaning: The array of scaled digits of the second input.
precision-recovery.quote: Here $u,v$ denote the scaled digit arrays (letters redefined): a digit $a$ is stored as $a2^{-b-2}$, norm under $1/4$.

precision-recovery.name: exact transform of u
precision-recovery.meaning: The exact source transform of u.
precision-recovery.quote: Let $U,V_1$ be their exact source transforms and $\widetilde U,\widetilde V_1$ the computed ones, of norm under $.26$.

precision-recovery.name: exact transform of v
precision-recovery.meaning: The exact source transform of v.
precision-recovery.quote: Let $U,V_1$ be their exact source transforms and $\widetilde U,\widetilde V_1$ the computed ones, of norm under $.26$.

precision-recovery.name: exact opposite transform
precision-recovery.quote: Both source Fourier transforms, $F$ and $F^+$, carry $1/S$, so $F(u*v)=S\,Fu\cdot Fv$ and $F^+F=I/S$; the retained permutation cancels ([Retained permutation cancellation](retained-permutations.md)), so the exact opposite transform $G$ gives $G(U\cdot V_1)=(u*v)/S^2$

precision-recovery.name: first-scaling error
precision-recovery.meaning: The error bound, in units of h_p, after multiplying by S.
precision-recovery.quote: Multiplying exactly by $S$, $\widetilde w$ approximates $w=(u*v)/S$ within $E_wh_p$:

precision-recovery.name: output digit
precision-recovery.quote: With $Q_0=2^b$ and $k_0=0$, output digit $d_j$ and carry $k_j$ satisfy

precision-recovery.name: carry
precision-recovery.quote: With $Q_0=2^b$ and $k_0=0$, output digit $d_j$ and carry $k_j$ satisfy

radix-digit-reduction.name: first input
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The first of the two integers being multiplied.

radix-digit-reduction.name: second input
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The second of the two integers being multiplied.

radix-digit-reduction.name: input bit length
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The number of bits in each input.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $n$ be the number of bits in each input, and let $b=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ be the number of bits in one digit, so $n\le 2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit width
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The number of bits in one radix digit.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $n$ be the number of bits in each input, and let $b=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ be the number of bits in one digit, so $n\le 2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: padded length
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: A power of two with 4n/b <= T < 8n/b.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: $T$ is the padded length, a power of two with $4n/b\le T<8n/b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: convolution length
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The length of the cyclic convolution, a product of distinct odd primes with T/2 < S < T.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: $S$ is the length of the cyclic convolution, a product of distinct odd primes with $T/2<S<T$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit count
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The number of radix-2^b digits in each input.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $q=\lceil n/b\rceil$ be the number of digits in each input, padding with leading zeros.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit of u
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The i-th radix-2^b digit of u, an integer below 2^b.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Write $u=\sum_{i=0}^{q-1}u_i2^{bi}$ and $v=\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}v_k2^{bk}$, where the digits $u_i$ and $v_k$ are integers with $0\le u_i,v_k<2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit of v
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The k-th radix-2^b digit of v, an integer below 2^b.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Write $u=\sum_{i=0}^{q-1}u_i2^{bi}$ and $v=\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}v_k2^{bk}$, where the digits $u_i$ and $v_k$ are integers with $0\le u_i,v_k<2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: polynomial variable
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The variable of the digit polynomials, evaluated at 2^b to recover the integers.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $x$ be a polynomial variable, and form the polynomials in $x$ with the $u_i$ and with the $v_k$ as coefficients.

radix-digit-reduction.name: product coefficient
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The coefficient of x^j in the product of the digit polynomials.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $c_j=\sum_{i+k=j}u_iv_k$ be the coefficient of $x^j$ in that product.

rank-recurrence.name: call parameter
rank-recurrence.meaning: The parameter of a recursive call: the number of digits per interchanged chunk, or the number of selected axes in a butterfly layer.
rank-recurrence.quote: A call has a parameter $f$, the number of digits per interchanged chunk or of selected axes, and a volume $V$.

rank-recurrence.name: slot count
rank-recurrence.meaning: The number of size-f slots into which a call at parameter mf cuts its parameter, equal to 10^6, the label-space dimension.
rank-recurrence.quote: A call at parameter $mf$, with $m=10^6$ (the label-space dimension) slots of size $f$, deals its rows into $W$ streams of volume $V/W$, one per wire of a fixed bit or complex [exchange network](exchange-network.md).

rank-recurrence.name: number of smaller calls
rank-recurrence.meaning: The number of calls at parameter f made by a call at parameter mf: the total rank of the frame changes over all edges of the network.
rank-recurrence.quote: So the call makes $s$ calls at parameter $f$, each on volume $V/W$, where $s$ is the total edge rank.

rank-recurrence.name: cost per unit volume
rank-recurrence.meaning: F(f) is the running time of a call at parameter f divided by the volume of its data.
rank-recurrence.quote: With $F(f)$ the time per unit volume at parameter $f$, these cost $s(V/W)F(f)$.

rank-recurrence.name: recursion depth
rank-recurrence.meaning: The number of recursion levels between the top call and the nodes considered.
rank-recurrence.quote: Unrolling through $\log_m f$ levels ($f$ a power of $m$), with depth $j$ (here counting levels) contributing $(s/W)^j$, gives $F(f)=O\big(\sum_{j=0}^{\log_m f}(s/W)^j\big)$.

rank-recurrence.name: saving exponent
rank-recurrence.meaning: A fixed exponent below 1 with s/W < m^tau, which makes an interchange cost O(V f^tau); here tau = 1 - 2^{-50}.
rank-recurrence.quote: If $s/W<m^\tau$ with fixed $\tau<1$, this is $O(f^\tau)$: if $s/W\le1$ there are $1+\log_m f$ terms of at most $1$; otherwise the last term, below $m^{\tau\log_m f}=f^\tau$, dominates the geometric sum.

rank-recurrence.name: relative rank deficit
rank-recurrence.meaning: The fraction (Wm - s)/(Wm) by which the number of smaller calls s falls short of Wm.
rank-recurrence.quote: Write $s/W=m(1-\eta)$, with $\eta$ now the relative deficit $(Wm-s)/(Wm)$.

retained-permutations.name: axis-length tuple
retained-permutations.meaning: The tuple $(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ of prime axis lengths, one per axis.

retained-permutations.name: padded-length tuple
retained-permutations.meaning: The tuple $(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ of power-of-two axis lengths.

retained-permutations.name: axis-length tuple
retained-permutations.meaning: A generic tuple of axis lengths.
retained-permutations.quote: For a tuple $\boldsymbol q$ of axis lengths, $F_{\boldsymbol q}=\bigotimes_iF_{q_i}$ is the normalized [discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) along every axis, and $F_{\boldsymbol q}^+$ its opposite.

retained-permutations.name: multidimensional transform
retained-permutations.meaning: The normalized discrete Fourier transform applied along every axis of an array with axis lengths q.
retained-permutations.quote: For a tuple $\boldsymbol q$ of axis lengths, $F_{\boldsymbol q}=\bigotimes_iF_{q_i}$ is the normalized [discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) along every axis, and $F_{\boldsymbol q}^+$ its opposite.

retained-permutations.name: time exponent
retained-permutations.meaning: The fixed exponent in the time bound of Gaussian resampling.
retained-permutations.quote: For one axis, with $p$ and $\alpha$ as there and $\delta$ the fixed exponent in its time bound, let $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$ ($u,v$ are complex arrays here, not integers).

retained-permutations.name: complex array
retained-permutations.meaning: Here a complex array, not an integer; changes meaning from the multiplication page.
retained-permutations.quote: For one axis, with $p$ and $\alpha$ as there and $\delta$ the fixed exponent in its time bound, let $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$ ($u,v$ are complex arrays here, not integers).

retained-permutations.name: complex array
retained-permutations.meaning: Here a complex array, not an integer; changes meaning from the multiplication page.
retained-permutations.quote: For one axis, with $p$ and $\alpha$ as there and $\delta$ the fixed exponent in its time bound, let $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$ ($u,v$ are complex arrays here, not integers).

retained-permutations.name: source permutation
retained-permutations.meaning: The tensor product of the source permutations P_{s_i}; a permutation, not the scalar ring.
retained-permutations.quote: Put $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$ (a permutation, not a ring), $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$.

retained-permutations.name: power-of-two exponent
retained-permutations.meaning: The exponent 2 d alpha^2 of the total scalar factor 2^gamma.
retained-permutations.quote: By the product rule the left sides combine to $RF_{\boldsymbol s}$, and the right sides to $\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A$ times $d$ factors $2^{2\alpha^2}$, so $RF_{\boldsymbol s}=2^\gamma\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A$ with $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$.

retained-permutations.name: largest axis length
retained-permutations.meaning: The largest axis length, a power of two 2^l.
retained-permutations.quote: With $t_i\in\{t_{\max}/2,t_{\max}\}$, $t_{\max}=2^\ell$, at most $2dT/t_{\max}$ lines occur, since $t_i\ge t_{\max}/2$, so setup $O(p^g)$ per line ($g$ a fixed exponent) totals $O(dTp^g/t_{\max})=o(Tp)$ when $t_{\max}$ outgrows every power of $p$ and $d$ is polynomially bounded in $p$.

retained-permutations.name: setup exponent
retained-permutations.meaning: A fixed exponent bounding per-line setup work by p^g.
retained-permutations.quote: With $t_i\in\{t_{\max}/2,t_{\max}\}$, $t_{\max}=2^\ell$, at most $2dT/t_{\max}$ lines occur, since $t_i\ge t_{\max}/2$, so setup $O(p^g)$ per line ($g$ a fixed exponent) totals $O(dTp^g/t_{\max})=o(Tp)$ when $t_{\max}$ outgrows every power of $p$ and $d$ is polynomially bounded in $p$.

retained-permutations.name: entry multi-index
retained-permutations.meaning: The index (j_1,...,j_d) of an entry of the array.

retained-permutations.name: unit
retained-permutations.meaning: An integer that is a unit (invertible) modulo q.
retained-permutations.quote: For a unit $c$ modulo $q$ and a vector $z$ of $q$ entries, let $(R_cz)_j=z_{cj}$.

retained-permutations.name: complex vector
retained-permutations.meaning: A vector of q complex entries.
retained-permutations.quote: For a unit $c$ modulo $q$ and a vector $z$ of $q$ entries, let $(R_cz)_j=z_{cj}$.

retained-permutations.name: axis operator
retained-permutations.meaning: An operator acting on vectors of length q_i, applied along axis i.
retained-permutations.quote: For operators $X_i$ acting on vectors of length $q_i$, $\bigotimes_iX_i$ acts on a $d$-axis array by applying $X_i$ along every line of axis $i$.

retained-permutations.name: second axis operator
retained-permutations.meaning: A further operator acting on vectors of length q_i, applied along axis i.
retained-permutations.quote: Operators on different axes touch different indices, so for further operators $Y_i$, $\bigl(\bigotimes_iX_i\bigr)\bigl(\bigotimes_iY_i\bigr)=\bigotimes_iX_iY_i$.

ring-convolution.name: number of records
ring-convolution.meaning: The number of polynomial records, one per cyclic address of the remaining axes.
ring-convolution.quote: Let $M=\prod_i t_i$ be the number of records, $T=rM$ the number of complex coefficients, and $*$ cyclic convolution.

ring-convolution.name: number of coefficients
ring-convolution.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in an array, T = rM.
ring-convolution.quote: Let $M=\prod_i t_i$ be the number of records, $T=rM$ the number of complex coefficients, and $*$ cyclic convolution.

ring-convolution.name: forward transform
ring-convolution.quote: Let $F^-$, $F^+$ be the forward and opposite synthetic transforms.

ring-convolution.name: opposite transform
ring-convolution.quote: Let $F^-$, $F^+$ be the forward and opposite synthetic transforms.

ring-convolution.name: pointwise product
ring-convolution.meaning: The pointwise product of records, P(u,v) = uv/r.

ring-convolution.name: layout permutation
ring-convolution.meaning: The permutation of records produced by the tape layout.
ring-convolution.quote: Perform both forward transforms and retain their common $LB$ order, with $L$ the layout permutation of records and $B$ the bit-reversal order.

ring-convolution.name: bit-reversal order
ring-convolution.meaning: The bit-reversal order in which forward outputs are written.
ring-convolution.quote: Perform both forward transforms and retain their common $LB$ order, with $L$ the layout permutation of records and $B$ the bit-reversal order.

ring-convolution.name: opposite map
ring-convolution.meaning: The exact counterpart F^+ B^{-1} L^{-1} of the opposite procedure.
ring-convolution.quote: Their exact counterparts are $LBF^-$ and the opposite map $\mathcal T_+=F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}$; permuting records preserves the norm, so $\mathcal T_+$ is a contraction.

ring-convolution.name: log of record length
ring-convolution.meaning: The base-2 logarithm of the record length r.
ring-convolution.quote: With $\ell=\log_2r$, each procedure maps disk grid arrays to disk grid arrays with error less than $\delta=\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$

ring-convolution.name: transform error
ring-convolution.meaning: The error bound sqrt2 * l * 2^{-p} of each forward or opposite procedure.
ring-convolution.quote: With $\ell=\log_2r$, each procedure maps disk grid arrays to disk grid arrays with error less than $\delta=\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$

ring-convolution.name: truncation error
ring-convolution.meaning: The error bound sqrt2 * 2^{-p} for one truncation.
ring-convolution.quote: truncated by $Q_p$ to $p$ bits of precision, which changes it by less than $\eta=\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ without raising the norm

ring-convolution.name: layout chunk width
ring-convolution.meaning: The width of the address chunks used by the tape layout.
ring-convolution.quote: Each transform, and the final linear scaling, costs $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}])$, with $K$ the layout chunk width and $\tau,\lambda'$ exponents from the cost lemma.

ring-y.name: ring variable
ring-y.meaning: The indeterminate of the polynomials; it satisfies y^r = -1 in the ring.
ring-y.quote: Write $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ for it, where $y$ is the ring variable, the indeterminate of the polynomials, and $r$ is the record length, the number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring, always a power of two with $r\geq 2$.

ring-y.name: record length
ring-y.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring, always a power of two.
ring-y.quote: Write $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ for it, where $y$ is the ring variable, the indeterminate of the polynomials, and $r$ is the record length, the number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring, always a power of two with $r\geq 2$.

ring-y.name: excess degree
ring-y.meaning: The number of places a term's degree exceeds r-1.
ring-y.quote: A term of degree $r+j$, where $j\geq 0$ is the number of places its degree exceeds $r-1$, is therefore replaced using $y^{r+j}=-y^j$: it wraps around to the front with its sign flipped.

ring-y.name: shift exponent
ring-y.meaning: An integer exponent of y by which an element is multiplied.

signed-packing.name: fractional bits
signed-packing.meaning: The number of fractional bits of each coefficient component.
signed-packing.quote: It multiplies in the [Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1](ring-y.md) in $O(rp\log(rp))$ time, where $p$ is the number of fractional bits of each coefficient.

signed-packing.name: ring
signed-packing.meaning: The ring of polynomials of degree below r modulo y^r+1.
signed-packing.quote: Let $f,g$ be polynomials of the ring, written $\mathcal R_r$, whose coefficients are $2^{-p}$ times Gaussian integers of modulus at most $2^p$, so coefficients have modulus at most $1$.

signed-packing.name: first polynomial
signed-packing.meaning: A polynomial of the ring with coefficients 2^{-p} times Gaussian integers.
signed-packing.quote: Let $f,g$ be polynomials of the ring, written $\mathcal R_r$, whose coefficients are $2^{-p}$ times Gaussian integers of modulus at most $2^p$, so coefficients have modulus at most $1$.

signed-packing.name: integer polynomial
signed-packing.meaning: Integer-coefficient polynomial, real part numerator of f (similarly b, c, e).
signed-packing.quote: Write $f=2^{-p}(a+ib)$ and $g=2^{-p}(c+ie)$, where $a,b,c,e$ are integer-coefficient polynomials of degree below $r$ with coefficients of absolute value at most $2^p$.

signed-packing.name: packing base
signed-packing.meaning: The base 2^{4p} at which polynomials are evaluated.
signed-packing.quote: Set $B_0=2^{4p}$, the packing base.

signed-packing.name: signed evaluation integer
signed-packing.meaning: The integer u(B_0) for u among a, b, c, e.
signed-packing.quote: For $u\in\{a,b,c,e\}$ with coefficients $u_j$, let $A_u=u(B_0)=\sum_{j<r}u_jB_0^j$ be the signed evaluation integer.

signed-packing.name: coefficient of u
signed-packing.meaning: The coefficient of y^j in u.
signed-packing.quote: For $u\in\{a,b,c,e\}$ with coefficients $u_j$, let $A_u=u(B_0)=\sum_{j<r}u_jB_0^j$ be the signed evaluation integer.

signed-packing.name: packing carry
signed-packing.meaning: The carry into block j when forming A_u, in {-1,0}.
signed-packing.quote: To form $A_u$, start with carry $\gamma_0=0$, let $d_j\in[0,B_0)$ be the residue of $u_j+\gamma_j$ modulo $B_0$, and put $\gamma_{j+1}=(u_j+\gamma_j-d_j)/B_0$.

signed-packing.name: packed block
signed-packing.meaning: The j-th block of 4p bits of the encoding of A_u, in [0,B_0).
signed-packing.quote: To form $A_u$, start with carry $\gamma_0=0$, let $d_j\in[0,B_0)$ be the residue of $u_j+\gamma_j$ modulo $B_0$, and put $\gamma_{j+1}=(u_j+\gamma_j-d_j)/B_0$.

signed-packing.name: product coefficient
signed-packing.meaning: The coefficient of y^j in an ordinary integer-polynomial product such as h=ac.
signed-packing.quote: For the ordinary product $h=ac$ of integer polynomials, $A_aA_c=(ac)(B_0)=\sum_{j<2r}h_jB_0^j$, padding $h_{2r-1}=0$.

signed-packing.name: product integer
signed-packing.meaning: One of the four product integers, equal to the sum of h_j B_0^j for its ordinary product h.
signed-packing.quote: Extraction takes one product integer $Z=\sum_{j<2r}h_jB_0^j$, where $h$ is its ordinary product.

signed-packing.name: block of Z
signed-packing.meaning: The j-th block of Z in sign-extended two's complement, in [0,B_0).
signed-packing.quote: Because $|Z|<B_0^{2r}/4$, write $Z=\sum_{j<2r}q_jB_0^j+\varepsilon B_0^{2r}$ with blocks $0\le q_j<B_0$ and $\varepsilon\in\{-1,0\}$.

signed-packing.name: sign extension
signed-packing.meaning: The sign-extension digit of Z, in {-1,0}.
signed-packing.quote: Because $|Z|<B_0^{2r}/4$, write $Z=\sum_{j<2r}q_jB_0^j+\varepsilon B_0^{2r}$ with blocks $0\le q_j<B_0$ and $\varepsilon\in\{-1,0\}$.

signed-packing.name: extraction carry
signed-packing.meaning: The carry into block j during extraction, in {0,1}.
signed-packing.quote: Put $\rho_0=0$ and let $\rho_j$ be the carry into block $j$.

signed-packing.name: extracted coefficient
signed-packing.meaning: The centered residue of q_j+rho_j modulo B_0, equal to h_j.
signed-packing.quote: Let $\widehat h_j$ be the unique integer in $[-B_0/2,B_0/2)$ congruent to $q_j+\rho_j$ modulo $B_0$

signed-packing.name: numerator coefficient
signed-packing.meaning: The Gaussian integer coefficient of y^j after reduction modulo y^r+1.
signed-packing.quote: Let $H_j$ be the resulting Gaussian integer coefficient.

signed-packing.name: first-factor index
signed-packing.meaning: The index of a coefficient of the first factor.
signed-packing.quote: For each $j_1$, the index of a coefficient of the first factor, exactly one $j_2$, the index of a coefficient of the second factor, has $j_1+j_2\equiv j\pmod r$, signed $+$ if $j_1+j_2=j$ and $-$ otherwise.

signed-packing.name: second-factor index
signed-packing.meaning: The index of a coefficient of the second factor.
signed-packing.quote: For each $j_1$, the index of a coefficient of the first factor, exactly one $j_2$, the index of a coefficient of the second factor, has $j_1+j_2\equiv j\pmod r$, signed $+$ if $j_1+j_2=j$ and $-$ otherwise.

simultaneous-layer.name: selected chunk count
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number of address chunks carrying a selected bit.
simultaneous-layer.quote: The simultaneous butterfly layer applies $H_0$ coefficientwise to one bit of each of $D\le d$ address chunks of $K$ bits $(d$ bounds their number) in time $O(Vd^{\lambda'}),$ $\lambda'<1,$ instead of $D$ passes.

simultaneous-layer.name: chunk bound
simultaneous-layer.meaning: An upper bound on the number of chunks a layer acts on.
simultaneous-layer.quote: The simultaneous butterfly layer applies $H_0$ coefficientwise to one bit of each of $D\le d$ address chunks of $K$ bits $(d$ bounds their number) in time $O(Vd^{\lambda'}),$ $\lambda'<1,$ instead of $D$ passes.

simultaneous-layer.name: record array
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The array of records, a function of the address x.
simultaneous-layer.quote: For records $z$ at addresses $x$ with selected bits $x_1,\dots,x_D,$ $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$ with $(\mathcal S_Dz)(x)=i^{x_1+\dots+x_D}z(x),$ all exact Gaussian dyadic: $b^D=(-i/2)^{\lfloor D/2\rfloor}b^{D\bmod2}$ is a shift, a phase and at most one factor $b.$

simultaneous-layer.name: address
simultaneous-layer.meaning: An address of the array, with selected bits x_1,...,x_D.
simultaneous-layer.quote: For records $z$ at addresses $x$ with selected bits $x_1,\dots,x_D,$ $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$ with $(\mathcal S_Dz)(x)=i^{x_1+\dots+x_D}z(x),$ all exact Gaussian dyadic: $b^D=(-i/2)^{\lfloor D/2\rfloor}b^{D\bmod2}$ is a shift, a phase and at most one factor $b.$

simultaneous-layer.name: phase diagonal
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The diagonal operator multiplying the record at address x by i^{x_1+...+x_D}.
simultaneous-layer.quote: For records $z$ at addresses $x$ with selected bits $x_1,\dots,x_D,$ $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$ with $(\mathcal S_Dz)(x)=i^{x_1+\dots+x_D}z(x),$ all exact Gaussian dyadic: $b^D=(-i/2)^{\lfloor D/2\rfloor}b^{D\bmod2}$ is a shift, a phase and at most one factor $b.$

simultaneous-layer.name: group axis count
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number of axes in a group, e = mf.
simultaneous-layer.quote: A group of $e=mf$ axes has $m$ slots of $f$ axes; a column holds one bit per slot, in $\mathbb F_2^m.$

simultaneous-layer.name: slot index
simultaneous-layer.meaning: Index of a slot, and of the residual basis vector placed on it.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Each edge changes frame by $\prod_hC_{v_h}^{\eta_h}$ per column (residual basis $v_h,$ $\eta_h=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v,$ $X_v$ shifting a column by $v).$

simultaneous-layer.name: residual vector
simultaneous-layer.meaning: A vector of a basis of the edge's residual space, in F_2^m.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Each edge changes frame by $\prod_hC_{v_h}^{\eta_h}$ per column (residual basis $v_h,$ $\eta_h=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v,$ $X_v$ shifting a column by $v).$

simultaneous-layer.name: edge sign
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The sign +1 or -1 of the kernel exponent attached to residual vector v_h.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Each edge changes frame by $\prod_hC_{v_h}^{\eta_h}$ per column (residual basis $v_h,$ $\eta_h=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v,$ $X_v$ shifting a column by $v).$

simultaneous-layer.name: shifted kernel
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The matrix aI+bX_v, the kernel C applied along the column direction v.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Each edge changes frame by $\prod_hC_{v_h}^{\eta_h}$ per column (residual basis $v_h,$ $\eta_h=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v,$ $X_v$ shifting a column by $v).$

simultaneous-layer.name: column shift
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The operator shifting the address of a column by v.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Each edge changes frame by $\prod_hC_{v_h}^{\eta_h}$ per column (residual basis $v_h,$ $\eta_h=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v,$ $X_v$ shifting a column by $v).$

simultaneous-layer.name: basis matrix
simultaneous-layer.meaning: An invertible binary m by m matrix whose first columns are the residual vectors v_h.
simultaneous-layer.quote: For invertible $G$ with first columns $v_h$ and $\mathcal P_G:x\mapsto Gx,$ $\mathcal P_GX_v\mathcal P_G^{-1}=X_{Gv}$

simultaneous-layer.name: basis permutation
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The address permutation moving a column value x to Gx.
simultaneous-layer.quote: For invertible $G$ with first columns $v_h$ and $\mathcal P_G:x\mapsto Gx,$ $\mathcal P_GX_v\mathcal P_G^{-1}=X_{Gv}$

simultaneous-layer.name: standard basis vector
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The h-th standard basis vector of F_2^m.
simultaneous-layer.quote: , so the edge change is $\mathcal P_G(\prod_hC_{e_h}^{\eta_h})\mathcal P_G^{-1}$ $(e_h$ standard basis).

simultaneous-layer.name: sign matrix
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The diagonal matrix diag(1,-1).
simultaneous-layer.quote: As $(C^{-1})^{\otimes f}=(-i)^fZ^{\otimes f}C^{\otimes f}Z^{\otimes f},$ $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1),$ inverse children need only signs and phases.

simultaneous-layer.name: row quotient
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The quotient of a row index on division by W.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Row $Wq+w$ (quotient $q,$ remainder $w<W)$ goes to wire role $w,$ so children have volume $V/W.$

simultaneous-layer.name: row remainder
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The remainder of a row index modulo W, which is the wire role.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Row $Wq+w$ (quotient $q,$ remainder $w<W)$ goes to wire role $w,$ so children have volume $V/W.$

simultaneous-layer.name: row chunk count
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number of leading chunks whose bits form the row index.
simultaneous-layer.quote: The first $q_0=\lceil\log_2W\rceil\lceil\log_m(2d)\rceil$ chunks, $q_0$ counting chunks, are done individually in $O(V\log d)$ (all chunks if $D\le q_0);$ their bits form a row index of range $2^{q_0K}\ge W^{\lceil\log_md\rceil},$ zero-padded at most doubling volume.

simultaneous-layer.name: step ratio
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The ratio s/W, at most m^sigma.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Take $\sigma<1$ with $\gamma=s/W\le m^\sigma,$ $K\le d^c$ $(c>0$ fixed), and $\lambda$ with $\max\{\tau,\sigma\}<\lambda<1,$ $\tau(1+c/\beta)<\lambda.$

simultaneous-layer.name: level index
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The index of a recursion level, counted from 0.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Levels indexed by $j\ge0$ sum to $O(e^\lambda)\sum_{j\ge0}(\gamma/m^\lambda)^j=O(e^\lambda).$

simultaneous-layer.name: leaf chunks
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number of active chunks in a leaf at level j, e/m^j.
simultaneous-layer.quote: A leaf at level $j$ has $u=e/m^j<d^\beta$ chunks and $\gamma^j\le(e/u)^\sigma,$ so leaves add $O(\gamma^ju)\le O(e^\sigma d^{\beta(1-\sigma)}).$

simultaneous-layer.name: piece digit
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The base-m digit of D-q_0 at position j, the number of pieces of m^j chunks.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Writing $D-q_0=\sum_ja_jm^j,$ $0\le a_j<m,$ gives $a_j$ pieces of $m^j$ chunks, at most $(m-1)(1+\lfloor\log_md\rfloor),$ hence a $\log(2d)$ factor:

simultaneous-layer.name: chain bound
simultaneous-layer.meaning: A(e) bounds the number of arithmetic operations on a chain from an input to an intermediate coefficient in a group of e axes.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Let $A(e)$ bound operations along a chain from an input to an intermediate coefficient.

simultaneous-layer.name: invocation bound
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The bound 64(W+m+1)^3 on operations added on a chain by one network invocation.
simultaneous-layer.quote: One invocation adds fewer than $E=64(W+m+1)^3$ (gates, corrections, $s<Wm),$ and chains concatenate the $s$ children:

simultaneous-layer.name: bound
simultaneous-layer.meaning: Any bound of at least 1 on the chain operation count.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Since $s\xi+E\le B\xi$ for $\xi\ge1,$ $B=s+E,$ over at most $\lceil\log_md\rceil$ levels, with $\nu=\min\{j\ge1:m^j\ge B\},$ $A(e)\le8B^2d^{\nu+1}.$

simultaneous-layer.name: recurrence base
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The sum s+E.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Since $s\xi+E\le B\xi$ for $\xi\ge1,$ $B=s+E,$ over at most $\lceil\log_md\rceil$ levels, with $\nu=\min\{j\ge1:m^j\ge B\},$ $A(e)\le8B^2d^{\nu+1}.$

simultaneous-layer.name: depth exponent
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The least j at least 1 with m^j at least B.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Since $s\xi+E\le B\xi$ for $\xi\ge1,$ $B=s+E,$ over at most $\lceil\log_md\rceil$ levels, with $\nu=\min\{j\ge1:m^j\ge B\},$ $A(e)\le8B^2d^{\nu+1}.$

simultaneous-layer.name: guard constant
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The constant 128mB^2 in the guard width.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Adding pieces, diagonals and $b^D$ stays below $\Delta=\lceil C_0d^{C_1}\rceil,$ $C_0=128mB^2,$ $C_1=\max\{20,\nu+3\}=20$ here.

simultaneous-layer.name: chain depth
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number of operations along a chain, the depth of a value.
simultaneous-layer.quote: For disk inputs on $2^{-p}\mathbb Z[i]$ and chain depth $\ell,$ values lie in $2^{-(p+\ell)}\mathbb Z[i]$ with modulus at most $2^\ell,$ by induction: addition doubles modulus, halving adds a denominator bit.

simultaneous-layer.name: axis exponent
simultaneous-layer.meaning: A fixed exponent with d = Theta(p^epsilon).
simultaneous-layer.quote: For $d=\Theta(p^\epsilon),$ fixed $\epsilon$ with $\epsilon C_1<1,$ $\Delta=o(p):$ width $O(p).$

stream-ops.name: array volume
stream-ops.meaning: The number of radix-q digits an array stores.
stream-ops.quote: Throughout, $V$ is the volume of an array, the number of radix-$q$ digits it stores, and $q\ge 2$ is the radix, the number of values one digit can take.

stream-ops.name: radix
stream-ops.meaning: The number of values one digit can take.
stream-ops.quote: Throughout, $V$ is the volume of an array, the number of radix-$q$ digits it stores, and $q\ge 2$ is the radix, the number of values one digit can take.

stream-ops.name: prefix values
stream-ops.meaning: The number of prefix values indexing the first axis of the array.
stream-ops.quote: In item 4 the array is indexed by $[P]\times[R]\times[B]$, where $P$ is the number of prefix values, $R$ is the number of rows (here $R$ is a row count, not the scalar ring) and $B$ is the number of entries per row.

stream-ops.name: row count
stream-ops.meaning: The number of rows in the array of item 4.
stream-ops.quote: In item 4 the array is indexed by $[P]\times[R]\times[B]$, where $P$ is the number of prefix values, $R$ is the number of rows (here $R$ is a row count, not the scalar ring) and $B$ is the number of entries per row.

stream-ops.name: entries per row
stream-ops.meaning: The number of entries in each row.
stream-ops.quote: In item 4 the array is indexed by $[P]\times[R]\times[B]$, where $P$ is the number of prefix values, $R$ is the number of rows (here $R$ is a row count, not the scalar ring) and $B$ is the number of entries per row.

stream-ops.name: stream count
stream-ops.meaning: The fixed number of streams the rows are dealt into.
stream-ops.quote: Dealing whole rows cyclically into $W$ streams, where $W$ is the fixed number of streams, and, when $W$ divides the number of rows, merging the streams in any fixed order of the row classes.

subspace-labels.name: number of smaller calls
subspace-labels.meaning: The total number of smaller calls that the edges of the network cost.
subspace-labels.quote: The labelling chooses the frames of [Frames on wire arrays](array-frames.md) so that $W$ wires cost $s<Wm$ smaller calls.

subspace-labels.name: wire count
subspace-labels.meaning: The number of wires of the network under consideration.
subspace-labels.quote: The labelling chooses the frames of [Frames on wire arrays](array-frames.md) so that $W$ wires cost $s<Wm$ smaller calls.

subspace-labels.name: one-factor label space
subspace-labels.meaning: The space $\mathbb Q^h$ with the form $x\cdot y-\frac19(\sum_ix_i)(\sum_iy_i)$ for the bit network, or $\mathbb F_2^h$ with the dot product for the complex network.
subspace-labels.quote: Bit labels live in $F=\mathbb Q^h$ with the nondegenerate form $\langle x,y\rangle=x\cdot y-\frac19(\sum_ix_i)(\sum_iy_i)$, complex ones in $F=\mathbb F_2^h$ with the dot product.

subspace-labels.name: a triple
subspace-labels.meaning: A three-element subset of $[h]$, used with $T$ to state the indicator inner products.
subspace-labels.quote: For *triples* (three-element subsets of $[h]$) $S,T$, the indicator vectors $t_S,t_T$ have integer dot product $|S\cap T|$ and entry sum $3$, so $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S\cap T|-1$; over $\mathbb F_2$, $t_S\cdot t_T=|S\cap T|\bmod 2$.

subspace-labels.name: a triple
subspace-labels.meaning: A three-element subset of $[h]$ (not the padded size used on other pages).
subspace-labels.quote: For *triples* (three-element subsets of $[h]$) $S,T$, the indicator vectors $t_S,t_T$ have integer dot product $|S\cap T|$ and entry sum $3$, so $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S\cap T|-1$; over $\mathbb F_2$, $t_S\cdot t_T=|S\cap T|\bmod 2$.

subspace-labels.name: triple indicator
subspace-labels.meaning: The indicator vector in $F$ of the triple $T$.
subspace-labels.quote: For *triples* (three-element subsets of $[h]$) $S,T$, the indicator vectors $t_S,t_T$ have integer dot product $|S\cap T|$ and entry sum $3$, so $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S\cap T|-1$; over $\mathbb F_2$, $t_S\cdot t_T=|S\cap T|\bmod 2$.

subspace-labels.name: ambient label space
subspace-labels.meaning: The space $F^{\otimes3}$, of dimension $m=h^3$, in which all labels lie.
subspace-labels.quote: Labels are built as [tensor products of subspaces](tensor-product-of-spaces.md) inside $\mathcal F=F^{\otimes3}$, of dimension $m=h^3$;

subspace-labels.name: X bank
subspace-labels.meaning: The bank of data wires $X_a$.
subspace-labels.quote: Banks $X$ and $Y$ hold the data wires $X_a,Y_a$, indexed by the $N$ tuples $a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)$ of triples.

subspace-labels.name: Y bank
subspace-labels.meaning: The bank of data wires $Y_a$.
subspace-labels.quote: Banks $X$ and $Y$ hold the data wires $X_a,Y_a$, indexed by the $N$ tuples $a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)$ of triples.

subspace-labels.name: triple tuple
subspace-labels.meaning: A tuple $(a_1,a_2,a_3)$ of triples indexing one data wire in each bank.
subspace-labels.quote: Banks $X$ and $Y$ hold the data wires $X_a,Y_a$, indexed by the $N$ tuples $a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)$ of triples.

subspace-labels.name: terminal line
subspace-labels.meaning: The line spanned by $t_{a_1}\otimes t_{a_2}\otimes t_{a_3}$, the source label of $X_a$.
subspace-labels.quote: With $U_a=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes t_{a_2}\otimes t_{a_3}\rangle$ the terminal labels are

subspace-labels.name: total dimension loss
subspace-labels.meaning: The total number of dimensions lost on decreasing edges.
subspace-labels.quote: If decreasing edges lose $L$ dimensions, absolute changes total $Wm-2N+2L$, so labels must keep $L$ small.

subspace-labels.name: stage number
subspace-labels.meaning: The stage, 1, 2 or 3, whose invocations act on coordinate $a_j$.
subspace-labels.quote: Stage $j$ acts on coordinate $a_j$.

subspace-labels.name: exposed factor space
subspace-labels.meaning: The tensor product $F^{\otimes(j-1)}$ of the factors exposed before stage $j$.
subspace-labels.quote: In one invocation put $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)},\ P=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle,\ B=P^\perp\cap A,\ K=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_3}\rangle$ (empty products are scalars).

subspace-labels.name: earlier tensor line
subspace-labels.meaning: The line spanned by $t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}$ inside $A$.
subspace-labels.quote: In one invocation put $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)},\ P=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle,\ B=P^\perp\cap A,\ K=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_3}\rangle$ (empty products are scalars).

subspace-labels.name: complement of P
subspace-labels.meaning: The orthogonal complement of $P$ inside $A$.
subspace-labels.quote: In one invocation put $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)},\ P=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle,\ B=P^\perp\cap A,\ K=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_3}\rangle$ (empty products are scalars).

subspace-labels.name: later tensor line
subspace-labels.meaning: The line spanned by $t_{a_{j+1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_3}$, tensored onto every label of stage $j$.
subspace-labels.quote: In one invocation put $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)},\ P=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle,\ B=P^\perp\cap A,\ K=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_3}\rangle$ (empty products are scalars).

subspace-labels.name: next exposed space
subspace-labels.meaning: The next stage's $A$, equal to $A\otimes F$.
subspace-labels.quote: It is the next stage's $B'$, for $A'=A\otimes F$ and $P'=P\otimes\langle t_{a_j}\rangle$; with $K=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes K'$ the outputs $A'\otimes\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes K'$ and $B'\otimes\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes K'$ are stage $j+1$'s inputs.

subspace-labels.name: next earlier line
subspace-labels.meaning: The next stage's $P$, equal to $P\otimes\langle t_{a_j}\rangle$.
subspace-labels.quote: It is the next stage's $B'$, for $A'=A\otimes F$ and $P'=P\otimes\langle t_{a_j}\rangle$; with $K=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes K'$ the outputs $A'\otimes\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes K'$ and $B'\otimes\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes K'$ are stage $j+1$'s inputs.

subspace-labels.name: next complement
subspace-labels.meaning: The next stage's $B$, the orthogonal complement of $P'$ in $A'$.
subspace-labels.quote: It is the next stage's $B'$, for $A'=A\otimes F$ and $P'=P\otimes\langle t_{a_j}\rangle$; with $K=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes K'$ the outputs $A'\otimes\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes K'$ and $B'\otimes\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes K'$ are stage $j+1$'s inputs.

subspace-labels.name: next later line
subspace-labels.meaning: The next stage's $K$, with $K=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes K'$.
subspace-labels.quote: It is the next stage's $B'$, for $A'=A\otimes F$ and $P'=P\otimes\langle t_{a_j}\rangle$; with $K=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes K'$ the outputs $A'\otimes\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes K'$ and $B'\otimes\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes K'$ are stage $j+1$'s inputs.

subspace-labels.name: X-bank indicator
subspace-labels.meaning: The indicator of the X-bank triple of a gate or wire in one invocation.
subspace-labels.quote: Suppressing $K$, with $t_X,t_Y$ indicators of the $X$- and $Y$-bank triples involved, wire labels (times bracketed) are

subspace-labels.name: Y-bank indicator
subspace-labels.meaning: The indicator of the Y-bank triple of a gate or wire in one invocation.
subspace-labels.quote: Suppressing $K$, with $t_X,t_Y$ indicators of the $X$- and $Y$-bank triples involved, wire labels (times bracketed) are

subspace-labels.name: bit dimension loss
subspace-labels.meaning: The total dimension lost on decreasing edges of the bit network.
subspace-labels.quote: With $I$ invocations of $c_{\rm b}$ centre wires, the bit loss is $L_{\rm b}=Ic_{\rm b}h$; as $I=3\binom h3^2$ and $N=\binom h3^3$, $L_{\rm b}/N=3c_{\rm b}h/\binom h3=100/539$, and likewise $L_{\rm c}/N=101/539$, both below $1/2$.

subspace-labels.name: complex dimension loss
subspace-labels.meaning: The total dimension lost on decreasing edges of the complex network.
subspace-labels.quote: With $I$ invocations of $c_{\rm b}$ centre wires, the bit loss is $L_{\rm b}=Ic_{\rm b}h$; as $I=3\binom h3^2$ and $N=\binom h3^3$, $L_{\rm b}/N=3c_{\rm b}h/\binom h3=100/539$, and likewise $L_{\rm c}/N=101/539$, both below $1/2$.

subspace-labels.name: projection onto a label
subspace-labels.meaning: The rational projection onto the label $U$ along $U^\perp$, the matrix of a bit-network vertex labelled $U$.
subspace-labels.quote: Bit vertices labelled $U$ get the projection $\Pi_U$ onto $U$ along $U^\perp$, except sources: $-\Pi_{U_a}$ at $X_a$, else $0$.

subspace-labels.name: bit smaller calls
subspace-labels.meaning: The number of smaller calls, the total rational rank of edge matrix changes, in the bit network.
subspace-labels.quote: So $s_{\rm b}=(W_{\rm b}m-2N+2L_{\rm b})+N=W_{\rm b}m-(N-2L_{\rm b})<W_{\rm b}m$.

subspace-labels.name: complex smaller calls
subspace-labels.meaning: The number of smaller calls, the total number of phase kernels, in the complex network.
subspace-labels.quote: [Binary phase frames](phase-frames.md) give the complex network $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}<W_{\rm c}m$.

synthetic-transform.name: transform length
synthetic-transform.meaning: The number of ring elements along one axis, a power of two dividing 2r.
synthetic-transform.quote: Let $t$ be the transform length, the number of ring elements along one axis, a power of two dividing $2r$.

synthetic-transform.name: two-adic exponent
synthetic-transform.meaning: The exponent of 2 in j when j is written as 2^e times an odd number.
synthetic-transform.quote: If $t\nmid j$, write $j$ as $2^e$ times an odd number, with $0\le e<\log_2 t$.

tensor-product-of-spaces.name: first space
tensor-product-of-spaces.meaning: The first of the two vector spaces being tensored.
tensor-product-of-spaces.quote: The tensor product $E\otimes G$ of two vector spaces $E$ and $G$ is a space of dimension $\dim E\cdot\dim G$ on which operators and bilinear forms of the two factors act factorwise.

tensor-product-of-spaces.name: second space
tensor-product-of-spaces.meaning: The second of the two vector spaces being tensored.
tensor-product-of-spaces.quote: The tensor product $E\otimes G$ of two vector spaces $E$ and $G$ is a space of dimension $\dim E\cdot\dim G$ on which operators and bilinear forms of the two factors act factorwise.

tensor-product-of-spaces.name: vector in E
tensor-product-of-spaces.meaning: A vector of the first space E.
tensor-product-of-spaces.quote: For vectors $\xi\in E$ and $\eta\in G$, the pure tensor $\xi\otimes\eta$ is defined by expanding bilinearly, so it is linear in $\xi$ and in $\eta$ separately.

tensor-product-of-spaces.name: vector in G
tensor-product-of-spaces.meaning: A vector of the second space G.
tensor-product-of-spaces.quote: For vectors $\xi\in E$ and $\eta\in G$, the pure tensor $\xi\otimes\eta$ is defined by expanding bilinearly, so it is linear in $\xi$ and in $\eta$ separately.

tensor-product-of-spaces.name: operator on E
tensor-product-of-spaces.meaning: A linear map from E to itself.
tensor-product-of-spaces.quote: For linear maps $\phi:E\to E$ and $\psi:G\to G$, the map $\phi\otimes\psi$ is the linear map with $(\phi\otimes\psi)(\xi\otimes\eta)=\phi(\xi)\otimes\psi(\eta)$.
